description: PyTorchFire is a Python wildfire model from its research developers that implements differentiable cellular automata in PyTorch. It provides simulation and parameter-calibration interfaces, with GPU execution available through PyTorch. Current examples accept harmonized terrain, fuel, wind and ignition layers and can use an observed final perimeter as a calibration target. Outputs are successive simulated fire states and calibrated model parameters. Spatial coverage and resolution follow the environmental arrays, while the simulation horizon is set through model steps. Source, a PyPI package, notebooks and API documentation are public and free under MIT. The tool can generate hazard scenarios relevant to emergency planning and infrastructure exposure, provided asset data are supplied separately. A limitation is that input quality and calibration choices control its usefulness; published speed comparisons do not establish accuracy for every fire. No directly related existing catalogue record was established. This review read documentation without installing the package, running a fire simulation or downloading its companion dataset.
